content:
anya: kicking off a focused GPTQ bake for three families: Llama2-13b, Mistral-7b-Instruct, Qwen-7b. goal: surface accuracy deltas + deployment profiles for GPTQ-4 vs AWQ-4 (and a small FP8 spotcheck). attached quick results and notes below.
victor: nice. what's the eval suite?
san jay: (sanjay) running MMLU / PIQA / HellaSwag / LAMBADA + a small regression harness (prod prompts subset).
mei: can you paste the exact command you used? useful for reproducing.
anya: sure — eval runner we used:
```
./eval_runner --model {model_path} --quant gptq-4 --tasks mmlu,piqa,hellaswag,lambada --batch 8 --max-seq 512 --kv-cache true --seed 42
```
anya: high-level summary:
- Llama2-13b GPTQ-4: avg relative delta vs fp16 = -0.9% across suite, but LAMBADA hit -2.4% (token-level). latency A100 p99: 18ms/token baseline fp16 16ms/token -> +12%
- Mistral-7b-Instruct GPTQ-4: avg delta = -0.4%, LAMBADA neutral, HellaSwag +0.3% (noise). latency A100 p99: 13ms/token fp16 12ms/token -> +8%
- Qwen-7b GPTQ-4: avg delta = -1.8%, notable regression on math prompts in prod subset, LAMBADA -3.6%. AWQ-4 for Qwen improved avg delta to -0.9% (but increased latency +6%).
victor: interesting that Mistral is holding up best. any idea why LAMBADA is sensitive on Llama2?
mei: likely scoring/tokenization edgecases + GPTQ reconstruction of final layers. we saw higher weight outliers in LM head during per-channel stats.
anya: ps — FP8 spotcheck (mistral, llama) looked promising: Mistral FP8 avg delta +0.1% (but unstable across seeds). we didn't push FP8 for Qwen yet.
ci-bot: deployment snapshot created: snap_id=20260316-gptq-bake-176999
olivia: memory profiles? what's the VRAM reduction for GPTQ-4 vs fp16?
san jay: rough numbers on A100-80GB:
- Llama2-13b fp16: 43GB -> gptq-4: 19GB -> ~56% reduction
- Mistral-7b fp16: 26GB -> gptq-4: 12GB -> ~54% reduction
- Qwen-7b fp16: 28GB -> gptq-4: 13GB -> ~54% reduction
anya: latency tradeoffs measured on A100 and T4 (single-request, kv-cache warm):
A100 p99 tokens/ms approximate:
- Llama2-13b fp16 0.0625 (16ms/token) -> gptq4 0.0556 (18ms/token)
- Mistral-7b fp16 0.0833 (12ms/token) -> gptq4 0.0769 (13ms/token)
- Qwen-7b fp16 0.0781 (12.8ms/token) -> gptq4 0.0694 (14.4ms/token)
T4 p99: quantized is relatively better due to memory bandwidth: gp4 latency gap smaller but throughput constrained.
victor: any regression patterns by head/ln? we should track for rollouts.
mei: yes — Llama2 final lm_head weights had higher quantization error (kurtosis), Mistral had flatter distribution which helps per-channel GPTQ. Qwen had some attention-kv scaling anomalies.
anya: practical recommendations for deploy profiles:
- Fast general-purpose: Mistral-7b GPTQ-4, can default to gptq with awq fallback for Qwen workloads.
- High-quality LAMBADA/long-span tasks: prefer fp16 for Llama2-13b or use AWQ-4 (tuned) — schedule canary with 10% traffic and regression hooks.
- Memory-constrained private deployment: GPTQ-4 gives ~50-60% VRAM savings; recommend larger KV cache tuning and reduced batch size.
olivia: can you add a short JSON summary for console ingestion? I'll wire up an automatic note in rollout playbooks.
anya: will do — plan to add per-model metric deltas + recommended fallback policies.
victor: thanks. please add a link to the raw eval logs and the small script that computes deltas.
anya: logs: https://s3.redwood-internal/prod-bakes/1769991234/ (raw.json.gz, diffs.csv). script: https://git.redwood/infra/evals/tools/compute_deltas.py
mei: flagged a followup: run AWQ-4 sweep on Llama2 8/16 group quant configs, and rerun Qwen with per-layer clip.
anya: noted — creating followup thread after this. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
